\chapter{O que ocorreu}
\label{ch:pt-o-que-ocorreu}
\hlchaptermodality{271}

\begin{chapteropening}

\section[ocorrer]{ocorrer — to occur, to happen}

\label{lesson:PT-C271-ocorrer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the moment that, then the Portuguese for suddenly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ocorrer}
\textbf{ocorrer} — \textquotedblleft{}to occur, to happen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O problema ocorreu durante a noite.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The problem occurred during the night.}
\end{quote}

Formal and frequent on the news; in speech, \emph{acontecer}. \emph{Ocorre-me uma ideia} — an idea occurs to me.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ocorrer} was borrowed from Latin \emph{occurrere} \textquotedblleft{}to run to meet, to come up\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{ob} \textquotedblleft{}towards\textquotedblright{} and \emph{currere} \textquotedblleft{}to run\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ocorrer}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ocorrer}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ocorrer}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the moment that, then the Portuguese for suddenly, then say \emph{ocorrer} again
\end{itemize}

What does ocorrer mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To occur, to happen\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[suceder]{suceder — to come after; to happen}

\label{lesson:PT-C271-suceder}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for suddenly, then the Portuguese for to occur.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: suceder}
\textbf{suceder} — \textquotedblleft{}to come after; to happen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O filho sucedeu ao pai na empresa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The son came after his father in the company.}
\end{quote}

\emph{O que sucedeu?} — what happened? With \emph{a}, it means to take someone’s place.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{suceder} comes from Latin \emph{succēdere} \textquotedblleft{}to come up after, to take the place of\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{sub} and \emph{cēdere} \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{suceder}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{suceder}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for suddenly, then the Portuguese for to occur, then say \emph{suceder} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[decorrer]{decorrer — to take place, to go on (over a stretch of time)}

\label{lesson:PT-C271-decorrer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to occur, then the Portuguese for to come after.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: decorrer}
\textbf{decorrer} — \textquotedblleft{}to take place, to go on (over a stretch of time)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A festa decorreu no jardim.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The party took place in the garden.}
\end{quote}

\emph{No decorrer de} means ‘as … goes on’: \emph{no decorrer do ano} — as the year went on.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{decorrer} is inherited from Latin \emph{dēcurrere} \textquotedblleft{}to run down, to run its course\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{dē} and \emph{currere} \textquotedblleft{}to run\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o acontecimento]{o acontecimento — the event, the happening}

\label{lesson:PT-C271-acontecimento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to come after, then the Portuguese for to take place.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o acontecimento}
\textbf{o acontecimento} — \textquotedblleft{}the event, the happening\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O concerto foi o grande acontecimento do verão.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The concert was the big event of the summer.}
\end{quote}

An important happening. Built on \emph{acontecer}, ‘to happen’.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{acontecimento} is built on \emph{acontecer} \textquotedblleft{}to happen\textquotedblright{}, which is usually traced to Latin \emph{contingere} \textquotedblleft{}to touch, to befall\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with the noun ending \emph{-mento}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a ocorrência]{a ocorrência — the incident, the occurrence}

\label{lesson:PT-C271-ocorrencia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to take place, then the Portuguese for the event.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a ocorrência}
\textbf{a ocorrência} — \textquotedblleft{}the incident, the occurrence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A polícia respondeu a uma ocorrência na rua de cima.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The police responded to an incident in the street above.}
\end{quote}

A police and news word for any reported incident.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ocorrência} is a learned noun built on \emph{ocorrer} \textquotedblleft{}to occur\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{occurrere} \textquotedblleft{}to run to meet\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), with the ending \emph{-ência}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
